title: Maximum Good Subarray Sum
summary: Given an array of numbers and a positive integer k, find the maximum sum of a subarray where the difference between the first and last elements is exactly k.
statement: Given an array of numbers and a positive integer k, find the maximum sum of a subarray where the difference between the first and last elements is exactly k. If no such subarray exists, return 0.
constraints: nums has at least two signed integers and k is positive.
A subarray is good when the absolute difference between its first and last values is exactly k.
Return the maximum good-subarray sum, including negative maxima, or zero if none exists.
hints: For a subarray ending at value v, its first value must be v-k or v+k, and the smallest earlier prefix maximizes the sum.
Track the minimum prefix immediately before every possible first value.
Before adding v, minimize prefix_by_value[v]; add v; test prefix-prefix_by_value[v±k].
Every good subarray is considered at its right endpoint, and choosing the minimum compatible starting prefix yields the maximum sum for that endpoint pair value.
editorial: Every good subarray is considered at its right endpoint, and choosing the minimum compatible starting prefix yields the maximum sum for that endpoint pair value.

tests.explanation: Among adjacent endpoint pairs differing by one, [5,6] has the largest sum eleven.
The good subarray [2,4,5] has sum eleven, exceeding the other valid choice.
